podcast.title: Dominance in UK Music (1989-1990)
podcast.body: At the end of the 1980s and early 1990s, a significant portion of the UK's musical movement was heavily concentrated in Manchester, experiencing the full explosion of the Manchester sound. This sound was still commercially resistant to dying by 1991, with Blur's debut album "Leisure" being criticized for still sounding like a remnant of this fading movement.

podcast.title: Decline (Early 1993)
podcast.body: In February 1993, the Manchester Sound, associated with bands like The Stone Roses and Happy Mondays, was "on the way out." "the Manchester Sound of the Stone Roses and the Happy Mondays was on the way out"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
